name: Oregon DSL Submerged Lands Enhancement Fund
summary: Biennial grants for projects that restore, enhance or protect the beds and banks of Oregon-owned waterways, including fish and wildlife habitat, water quality and removal of derelict structures and marine debris. Nonprofits, watershed councils, Tribes and public bodies can apply, with a 25% match.

eligibility.rule: Project is not associated with compensatory mitigation requirements

documents: Street or highway location map with road directions
Assessor map containing the riparian uplands
Scaled drawing of existing and proposed structures and activity
Legal description and delineation of the work area
Work Plan or Operation & Maintenance Plans, if prepared

calls.label: 2025-27 grant cycle
calls.note: The funder says applications for 2027-29 will be announced later; no date is stated.

status.quote: Applications for the 2025-27 grant cycle closed on April 30, 2026.

applicant_types.quote: State agencies, city or county governments, federally recognized Tribes, water improvement districts, watershed councils, park and recreation districts, ports, and non-profit organizations.

geography.quote: Projects that enhance the beds and banks of Oregon-owned waterways often benefit water quality, surrounding wildlife, and waterway users.

access.quote: Subscribe to our "Waterways and Wetlands" list to be notified when applications open for 2027-29!

co_finance_required.quote: A 25% funding match is required for all projects not initiated by DSL (in-kind or cash).

eligibility.quote: Federal agencies are not eligible to receive funds.
Projects associated with compensatory mitigation requirements are not eligible for funding.

co_finance.quote: A 25% funding match is required for all projects not initiated by DSL (in-kind or cash).

documents.quote: A street or highway location map with road directions to the site from the nearest main highway or road. Assessor map that contains the riparian uplands. Do not mark on this map. A separate drawing to a scale of 1 inch = 100 feet of all existing and proposed structures and activity.

A legal description of the work area with an accurate delineation of the area relative to the tax lot boundaries of the upland parcel. (The Department may require a survey for this purpose). e) Project schedule including beginning and completion. f) Itemized Project Budget, including use of requested funds and contributing match funds.
All Work Plan or Operation & Maintenance Plans that have been prepared for the proposed activities. h) Confirmation of contributing match.
